title: Joint Tertiary SRC allowance petition submission (possible in-person gathering)
scope: Potential collective petition-submission action over government tertiary-student living allowances. The January Gazette says students were not rowdy when they submitted the petition; public-demonstration character, venue and headcount are not specified. A separate larger street demonstration was still described as looming in February.
organizer: Joint Tertiary Student Representative Council (SRCs from 18 tertiary schools, per the February follow-up); January report refers to tertiary institutions.
participants_original: Unknown. The February report says the Joint Tertiary SRC comprised SRCs from 18 tertiary schools; neither source gives the number present at petition submission. “Not rowdy” is not a count.
threshold_50_evidence: No attendance estimate is reported. Representation from 18 schools is not a participant count, and the January description does not clarify whether the petition was submitted by a public gathering. The ≥50 threshold remains unestablished.

title.summary: The January Gazette describes a recent tertiary-institution petition; the February follow-up identifies the Joint Tertiary Student Representative Council.

start_date.summary: The 17 February follow-up says the council made the demand at the start of 2022; the 19 January issue calls the petition recent. Only month-level January timing is supported; exact submission date is unknown.

end_date.summary: No physical end or duration of a petition-submission gathering is reported.

location.summary: The February follow-up says a petition was apparently submitted to the Ministry but names no venue. No gathering location is specified.

scope.summary: The January issue says petitioners were “not rowdy when they submitted the petition,” suggesting an in-person group may have been involved. The February article describes an even larger demonstration as still looming on 17 February, so that future demonstration is not assigned to January.

organizer.summary: February source names the Joint Tertiary SRC, comprising SRCs from 18 tertiary schools; the number of people at submission is unknown.

demands.summary: A 35% increase to tertiary-student living allowances to meet cost of living; February source states P2200 off-campus/P1700 on-campus. Coded as a state decision/domestic allowance policy, not a private wage dispute.

participants_original.summary: No headcount or attendance description. Eighteen schools describe organizational representation, not turnout.

threshold_50_evidence.summary: Neither source estimates attendance; “not rowdy” and the number of schools do not establish 50 participants.

protester_violence.summary: No protester violence is described; silence does not establish no violence.

state_response.summary: The January article says government intended to meet SRCs before week-end, while the February follow-up says students had not received feedback. No completed meeting or formal agreement to address demands is established; all seven responses remain unknown.

notes: This is an unresolved petition-submission lead rather than a confirmed mass demonstration. The Gazette’s printed p.3 wording that students were “not rowdy when they submitted the petition” suggests an in-person group, but does not establish a public gathering, venue or ≥50 attendees. The February follow-up (17 Feb, lines 108–121) dates the demand to the start of 2022 and says the “biggest demonstration” was still looming then; that planned future action is not assigned to January. Keep this state allowance policy issue separate from the private Mupane wage/bonus dispute.
open_questions: On what exact day was the petition submitted, and was it delivered by a public gathering or by representatives/correspondence?
Where was the submission and how many people were present simultaneously?
Was any distinct public demonstration held in January, or was only a petition submission reported?
Did the planned ministerial meeting occur and did officials formally agree to address the demand?
